bib.title: Finite-time Analysis of the Multiarmed Bandit Problem

question: Can logarithmic regret for the stochastic K-armed bandit be achieved uniformly over time (finite n), not only asymptotically, with simple and efficient policies?
hypothesis: Simple index policies based on Chernoff-Hoeffding confidence bounds, and a decaying-epsilon greedy rule, achieve uniform logarithmic regret for bounded rewards.
contributions: UCB1: index policy with logarithmic regret uniformly over n, rewards in [0,1] (Theorem 1)
UCB2: more complex policy whose leading constant approaches 1/(2 Delta^2) (Theorem 2)
epsilon_n-greedy with epsilon_n = cK/(d^2 n) with logarithmic regret bound (Theorem 3)
UCB1-NORMAL for Gaussian rewards with unknown means and variances (Theorem 4, relies on two numerically verified conjectures)
Empirical comparison of UCB1-TUNED, UCB2 and epsilon_n-greedy on Bernoulli bandits

method.summary: Theoretical paper with a small simulation study. Proves finite-time expected-regret bounds for UCB1, UCB2, epsilon_n-greedy and UCB1-NORMAL, then simulates UCB1-TUNED, UCB2 and epsilon_n-greedy on 2-armed and 10-armed Bernoulli bandits.

models.name: UCB1-TUNED
models.architecture: index policy; index uses sqrt((ln n / n_j) * min{1/4, V_j(n_j)}) with V_j(s)=(1/s)sum X^2 - xbar^2 + sqrt(2 ln t / s)

models.name: UCB1
models.architecture: play arm maximising xbar_j + sqrt(2 ln n / n_j) (confidence term stated in Sec 4 and proof c_{t,s}=sqrt(2 ln t / s)); pseudocode is in Fig 1 (image)

models.name: UCB2
models.architecture: epochs; arm maximising xbar_i + a_{n,r_i}, a_{n,r}=sqrt((1+alpha) ln(e n/tau(r)) / (2 tau(r))), tau(r)=ceil((1+alpha)^r); arm then played tau(r+1)-tau(r) times

models.name: epsilon_n-greedy
models.architecture: with prob 1-eps_n play empirical best, else random arm; eps_n=min(1, cK/(d^2 n))

limits: UCB1 constant 8/Delta^2 is worse than the Lai-Robbins constant; only UCB2 approaches 1/(2 Delta^2) and needs n >= 1/(2 Delta^2) and small alpha.
epsilon_n-greedy needs a known gap lower bound d, and c has no universal value; performance degrades rapidly when mistuned.
UCB1-TUNED, the best-performing UCB variant empirically, has no regret bound.
UCB1-NORMAL proof rests on two conjectures verified only numerically.
Rewards must have known bounded support [0,1] (Thm 1-3); stationary arms only, non-stationary and Gittins-type extensions are open.
Experiments are only Bernoulli with 2 or 10 arms; single 100-run averages, no variance reported in the text.
